- If sentiment history shows a final 1.00 (positive sentiment), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- Model consistently overestimates early in 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to first 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak for 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits mean-reversion bias — forecast tends to be too low; add 0.5–1.5% to mean of recent 5–7 days.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after a high, model often fails to recognize it; apply lag correction: delay forecast drop by 1–2 days, then reduce by 1–2% per day.
- For 30-day forecasts, model underestimates late-period prices (last 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% for final 5 days.
